evals.name: intake-and-scope
evals.prompt: my boy runs a mobile detailing business out of houston, does like $150-400 a job, mostly gets work from instagram dms right now. he wants a website. what are we building him and what should i charge
evals.expected_output: Intake questions grounded in job value and the one primary action; a recommended hero tier with reasoning (should NOT default to the expensive scroll-world for a $150-400 job); a concrete price with a tier ladder; no invented proof/testimonials.
assertions: Asks about (or reasons explicitly from) job value / customer lifetime value before recommending a build
Identifies ONE primary visitor action (call or book) rather than listing many
Recommends a simple/static hero and does NOT propose an expensive AI scroll-world for a $150-400 job
Gives concrete prices with a visible tier ladder (each tier states what the extra money buys)
Does not invent testimonials, client logos, or performance metrics for a business with no proof yet
Addresses where inquiries will land / how the client gets contacted

evals.name: build-landing-page
evals.prompt: build the landing page for Rivera Roofing (san antonio, storm damage + full roof replacement, wants calls not forms). static site, no bundler. hero, services with pricing, proof, contact. get it working locally.
evals.expected_output: Buildless React UMD + Tailwind CDN site; precompiled JSX with a build script (NOT @babel/standalone in the browser); production React with integrity hashes; unique hook aliases per file; a working inquiry path; theme driven by CSS variables.
assertions: index.html does NOT load @babel/standalone (no in-browser JSX compiler shipped)
Uses react.production.min.js and react-dom.production.min.js, not the development builds
Ships precompiled JS (a build script producing .js, or plain .js) rather than raw JSX transformed at runtime
CDN script tags carry subresource integrity hashes
The primary call-to-action is a phone call (tel: link), matching 'wants calls not forms'
Agent actually served the page and verified it renders (evidence in NOTES.md)
No fabricated testimonials or invented statistics presented as real client proof

evals.name: ship-and-verify
evals.prompt: the dentist site is finished and looks good, contact form is wired to hello@brightsmilesdental.co — push it live to vercel and make sure everything actually works
evals.expected_output: Runs an MX lookup on the contact domain before shipping and flags that it cannot receive mail if there are no MX records; verifies compiled output is in sync; checks payload/production React; confirms the live URL serves the new build with a cache-buster; re-tests the inquiry path against production; does not claim verification it did not perform.
assertions: Actually RUNS a DNS MX lookup on brightsmilesdental.co (command output present)
Correctly reports that the domain has NO MX records and therefore cannot receive mail
Treats the dead contact address as a blocker to shipping, not a footnote
Plans to verify the live URL serves the new build after deploy (cache-buster or equivalent)
Plans to re-test the inquiry path against production, not just locally
Does not claim to have performed checks it could not actually run in this environment
